home_check_unbalanced: Trial balance is not balanced. Please check vouchers!
voucher_balance_rule: Every debit must have a corresponding credit
voucher_balance_hint: The fundamental rule of double-entry bookkeeping: every transaction must be recorded as a debit in one account and a credit in another, with equal amounts.
voucher_no_entries: Please add at least two entries
ledger_explanation: A general ledger is a summarized record of transactions by account, showing the changes and balances for each account over a period. It is the primary basis for preparing financial statements.
reports_trial_balance_hint: A trial balance checks whether total debits equal total credits across all accounts. If they are not equal, there is a recording error.
reports_income_hint: The income statement shows business performance over a period. Revenue - Expenses = Profit.
reports_balance_hint: The balance sheet shows financial position at a point in time. Assets = Liabilities + Equity.
settings_reset_confirm: Reset all data? This will clear all vouchers and restore default accounts and knowledge cards.
practice_err_amount: Amount does not match the case
practice_s1_desc: Withdraw 5,000 from the bank for petty cash.
practice_s1_exp: Debit Cash on Hand (asset ↑), credit Bank Deposit (asset ↓).
practice_s2_exp: Debit Raw Materials, credit Accounts Payable.
practice_s3_desc: Sell goods 35,000; cash deposited to bank.
practice_s3_exp: Debit Bank Deposit, credit Main Operating Revenue.
practice_s4_exp: Debit Administrative Expenses, credit Cash on Hand.
practice_s5_exp: Debit Admin Expenses, credit Accumulated Depreciation.
practice_s6_exp: Debit Payroll Payable, credit Bank Deposit.
practice_s7_exp: Debit Main Operating Cost, credit Finished Goods.
practice_s8_desc: Close Main Operating Revenue 35,000 to Current Year Profit.
practice_s8_exp: Debit Revenue, credit Current Year Profit.
practice_s9_exp: Debit Selling Expenses, credit Bank Deposit.
practice_s10_desc: Owner invests 100,000 into the bank account.
practice_s10_exp: Debit Bank Deposit, credit Paid-in Capital.
closing_intro_body: Close P&L accounts into Current Year Profit, then move net profit to Profit Distribution so income/expense restart at zero next period.
closing_intro_steps: 3 steps: ① close revenue ② close expenses ③ close profit
closing_step_revenue_desc: Transfer credit balances of revenue accounts to Current Year Profit.
closing_step_expense_desc: Transfer debit balances of expense accounts to Current Year Profit.
closing_step_loss_desc: Net loss @loss covered from Profit Distribution.
closing_done_body: P&L accounts are zeroed and profit moved to distribution. Check the voucher list.
voucher_select_account_error: Select an account for every line
backup_hint: Export the full book (accounts, vouchers, practice progress) as JSON. Paste the backup content to restore.
backup_import_hint: Paste the full contents of the backup JSON file. Import overwrites current accounts and vouchers.
reports_cash_flow_hint: Simplified direct-method statement of operating, investing and financing cash flows. Closing cash should match the balance sheet.
cf_operating: I. Cash flows from operating activities
cf_investing: II. Cash flows from investing activities
cf_financing: III. Cash flows from financing activities
cf_sales_receipts: Cash received from sales of goods/services
cf_other_op_in: Other cash received from operating activities
cf_purchase_paid: Cash paid for goods and services
cf_wages_paid: Cash paid to and for employees
cf_other_op_out: Other cash paid for operating activities
cf_op_net: Net cash flow from operating activities
cf_invest_asset: Cash paid/received for fixed and intangible assets
cf_inv_net: Net cash flow from investing activities
cf_fin_net: Net cash flow from financing activities
cf_net_increase: Net increase in cash and cash equivalents
cf_opening_cash: Add: opening cash and cash equivalents
cf_reconcile_hint: Difference vs opening + net change (includes unclassified or internal transfers)
practice_s11_desc: Provide 2,000 for doubtful accounts at period end.
practice_s11_exp:
Dr. Impairment loss 2,000
Cr. Bad debt provision 2,000

The provision is a contra-asset to accounts receivable; it raises current expense and lowers AR carrying amount.
practice_s12_desc: Write off an uncollectible receivable of 3,000.
practice_s12_exp:
Dr. Bad debt provision 3,000
Cr. Accounts receivable 3,000

Writing off uses the existing provision and does not hit the income statement.
practice_s13_desc: Pay 15,000 advance to a supplier under contract.
practice_s13_exp:
Dr. Prepayments 15,000
Cr. Bank deposit 15,000

Prepayment is an asset — a claim for goods not yet received.
practice_s14_desc: Receive 12,000 from a customer before delivering goods.
practice_s14_exp:
Dr. Bank deposit 12,000
Cr. Advances from customers 12,000

Advances are a liability — an obligation to deliver.
practice_s15_desc: Borrow 80,000 from a bank for 6 months.
practice_s15_exp:
Dr. Bank deposit 80,000
Cr. Short-term borrowings 80,000

Short-term borrowings are current liabilities due within one year.
practice_s16_desc: Accrue 1,500 interest on the short-term loan (unpaid).
practice_s16_exp:
Dr. Finance expense 1,500
Cr. Interest payable 1,500

Accrual raises expense and liability; payment later clears the payable.
practice_s17_desc: Pay 5,600 VAT payable from last month.
practice_s17_exp:
Dr. Taxes payable — VAT 5,600
Cr. Bank deposit 5,600

Payment clears the tax liability.
practice_s18_desc: Sell surplus materials; 4,000 deposited to bank.
practice_s18_exp:
Dr. Bank deposit 4,000
Cr. Other operating revenue 4,000

Material sales go to other operating revenue, not main revenue.
practice_s19_desc: Purchase equipment not needing installation for 50,000 cash.
practice_s19_exp:
Dr. Fixed assets 50,000
Cr. Bank deposit 50,000

Capitalise the asset; depreciation starts next month.
practice_s20_desc: Close 9,000 admin expense to current-year profit.
practice_s20_exp:
Dr. Current-year profit 9,000
Cr. Admin expense 9,000

Period-end moves expense balances into current-year profit.
practice_s21_desc: Purchase a patent for 30,000 paid by bank.
practice_s21_exp:
Dr. Intangible assets 30,000
Cr. Bank deposit 30,000

Intangibles are amortised over their useful life.
practice_s22_desc: Sell goods and receive a commercial acceptance bill of 20,000.
practice_s22_exp:
Dr. Notes receivable 20,000
Cr. Main operating revenue 20,000

Notes receivable arise from commercial bills received on sales.
chapter_locked_hint: Pass every drill in the previous chapter to unlock this one.
chapter_1_sub: Cash withdraw, advances, material sales basics
chapter_2_sub: Purchases, sales, notes, prepayments and bad debts
chapter_4_sub: VAT payment, short-term loans and interest
chapter_6_sub: Close COGS, revenue and current-year profit
achievement_quiz_ready_desc: Pass 5 drills to unlock full quizzes
reports_ratios_hint: A few key ratios for solvency, structure and profitability. Teaching figures only.
ratio_intro: Current/quick ratio → short-term solvency; debt ratio → leverage; margins → profitability.
ratio_current_hint: Current assets / current liabilities. Around 2 is often considered safe.
ratio_quick_hint: (Current assets − inventory) / current liabilities. Excludes slow-moving inventory.
ratio_debt_hint: Total liabilities / total assets. Lower means less leverage.
ratio_inventory_hint: COGS / inventory. Higher means faster stock turns.
yearend_hint: Close revenue → expenses → transfer profit → accrue 10% surplus reserve.
yearend_intro: This workbench closes the full-year P&L and accrues 10% statutory surplus reserve.
yearend_skip_reserve: No profit this year — no surplus reserve needed.
yearend_summary_revenue: Year-end: close annual revenue to current-year profit
yearend_summary_expense: Year-end: close annual expenses to current-year profit
yearend_summary_profit: Year-end: transfer current-year profit to retained earnings
voucher_template_close_exp_desc: Close admin expense to current-year profit
kq_k1_a0: Every debit has a credit; they must be equal
kq_k1_e: Every debit has a credit of equal amount — the basis of trial balance.
kq_k2_e: Assets = Liabilities + Equity — foundation of the balance sheet.
kq_k4_q: Standard VAT rate for goods (general taxpayer)?
kq_k4_e: Sales of goods / processing use the 13% standard rate.
kq_k6_a0: Close revenue accounts to current-year profit
kq_k8_q: Does a balanced trial balance guarantee correctness?
kq_k8_e: A balanced trial balance is not fully correct: omissions, duplicates and wrong accounts can still balance.
kq_k21_q: When recognising sales revenue, the credit account is?
kq_k21_e: Sale: Dr bank/AR, Cr main operating revenue.
review_grade_label: How well did you know it?
kq_k3_q: Withdraw cash from bank — credit which account?
kq_k3_e: Dr cash on hand, Cr bank deposit.
kq_k7_q: FA added this month — when does depreciation start?
kq_k7_a2: Next month (not in the add month)
kq_k7_e: FA added this month: depreciation starts next month.
kq_k10_q: Net profit flows into which balance-sheet item?
kq_k10_e: Net profit → retained earnings links the three statements.
kq_k13_q: Accounts receivable is asset or liability?
kq_k13_e: AR is an asset — a claim for unpaid sales.
kq_k15_e: Accumulated depreciation is a contra-asset to fixed assets.
kq_k23_q: When paying wages, payroll payable is on which side?
kq_k23_e: Payment: Dr payroll payable, Cr bank — liability decreases.
kq_k54_q: Closing expenses to current-year profit — which side for profit?
kq_k54_e: Close expenses: Dr current-year profit, Cr expense.
kq_t1_e: General method: VAT payable = output − input VAT.
kq_t2_q: Preferential CIT rate for small/micro enterprises?
csv_import_hint: Paste CSV text. Simple two-line form or multi-line grouped by voucher_id.
